correctness.rationale: A paired selected set S corresponds to edge graph H with tau(H)>=3, since any two-vertex cover would be an uncovered pair and cannot be selected when S has an induced perfect matching. In four edges, the only tau>=3 shapes with perfect matching are 4K2, P3+2K2 and P4+K2, established via the triangle obstruction and Konig bipartite matching/cover equality. Direct labeled counts give 105,315,180. At n=5, six-edge S has four-edge complement B; tau>=3 iff B triangle-free, and four-edge triangle-free B is a tree or C4+isolated. C4+isolated has two forced matching edges with the same only partner; each three tree types admits an explicit perfect matching, giving Cayley 125. At n=4 KG is 3K2. Exhaustive independent graph verifier confirms every subset n=4..7 and every four-set n=8. No finite extrapolation is used.

value.rationale: Minimum paired domination and number of minimum configurations are fundamental graph invariants. The Petersen minimum sets have a structural bijection with labeled spanning trees, revealing a nonobvious 125 count; the infinite two-subset Kneser family has exactly three optimal auxiliary isomorphism types and a degree-eight binomial-basis count. This goes beyond the known minimum-size value at Petersen and the separate total-domination obstruction list without requiring an unsupported downstream conjecture.
